annotations.title: Pentecoſt.
annotations.text: [1] Though the Apoſtles might deſire to come to the Iewes Feſtiuities, by reaſon of the general concourſe of people to the ſame, the better to deale for their ſaluation and to ſpred the Goſpel of Chriſt, yet it is like that they now kept ſolemly the Chriſtian Pentecoſt or whitſontide, for memorie of the Holy Ghoſt, and that S. Paul vvent to that Feaſt of the Chriſtians rather then the other of the Ievves. And Ven. Bede ſaith here, The Apoſtle maketh haſt to keepe the fifteth day, that is, of remiſsion and of the Holy Ghoſt. For, that the Chriſtians already kept the eight day, that is, the [2] Sunday or our Lordes day, and had altered already the ordinarie Sabboth into the ſame, it is plaine by the Scriptures (1 Cor. 16, 2. Apoc. 1, 10.) and by antiquitie. Iuſtin. Mart. Apolog. 2 ad Anton. Pium in fine. And it is as like that they changed the Ievves Paſche and Pentecoſt as that, ſpecially when it is euident that [3] theſe Feſtiuities be kept by Apoſtolike tradition, and approued by the vſe of al auncient Churches and Councels.

annotations.title: Rauening vvolues.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> The gouernours of the Church are foretold of the great danger that ſhould fall to the people by vvolues, that is to ſay, by Heretikes, vvhoſe cruelty tovvard the Catholikes is noted by this terme. They be knowen by the forſaking the vnitie of the Church whereof they were before, by going out and dravving many diſciples after them, and by their peruerſe doctrine. Such vvolues came afterward in deede in diuers ages, Arius, Macedonius, Neſtorius, Eutyches, Luther, Caluin, great bloudſucking vvolues, and vvaſters of the flocke of Chriſt.

notes.text: Rauening wolues are the Heretikes of al ages.

annotations.title: It is a more bleſſed thing to giue.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> Among many other infinite goodly things and ſpeaches vvhich Chriſt ſpake and be not vvritten in the Goſpels, this ſentence is one: which S. Paul heard of ſome of the Apoſtles daily conuerſant vvith him, or els learned of Chriſt him ſelf, or of the Holy Ghoſt. And it ſignifieth, that whereas the vvorld commonly counteth him happie that receiueth any benefite, as almes either temporal or ſpiritual, <mn>[2]</mn> yet in deede he that giueth or beſtovveth, is more happie. Which if the vvorld did wel conſider, men would giue almes faſter then they do, if it were but for their owne benefite.

notes.text: Christs speaches not written in the Gospel.
